references.text: Esau settled in the Seir mountains, confirming that God gave this land to Esau's descendants as an inheritance.
Jacob sent messengers to his brother Esau in the land of Seir, in the region of Edom, showing Esau's connection to this territory.
Confirms that Esau received the Seir mountains as his inheritance, in accordance with God's promise.
A parallel command not to attack Moab, because God also gave them their land as an inheritance—the same principle as with Edom.
A similar command regarding the Ammonites, who also received their land as an inheritance from God—demonstrating God's sovereignty over the territories of nations.
Isaac's blessing to Esau, where he is promised a dwelling in fertile land, fulfilled by his receiving Seir.
Edom refused Israel passage through its land, so Israel had to go around it—related to the command not to fight against them.
A prophecy concerning Edom and the Seir mountains, showing the continued connection between Esau's descendants and this territory.
